newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00-2.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00-2.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 to 2.00 cents lower Wednesday as traders expect the market to follow through on its two-day run-up.

The New York arabica market vaulted to new contract highs across the board Tuesday as supply worries continued to dominate the market. July futures finished up 11.50 cents at 241.15 cents a lb after trading from a new lifetime high of 243.00 to 231.55. Spot May jumped 15.35 cents to 261.00 cents, while the back months closed 5.50 to 10.75 higher.
The July/September switch ballooned to 25.95 cents compared with 25.20 cents at the close on Friday.
Technically, traders said July would face some resistance at its lifetime high hit yesterday of 243.00, then 245.00 and 250.00. Light support was seen near 240.00.

Long-term weather outlooks for top-grower Brazil call for warm temperatures through Tuesday, Weather Services Corp said Wednesday. A high pressure system could move colder weather into southern or central Argentina late next week, but it is too early to forecast its effects on Brazil, they said.

"I see no significant changes (in Brazil) through the next seven days," said Weather Services Corp. senior meterologist Joel Burgio. "There's no sign the high is moving towards Brazil. Whether it will get into Argentina is even questionable."

After Tuesday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks continued to climb. Stocks increased by 1,745 bags, to 33,037 bags as of May 10. There were 16,435 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
In other news, industry sources in Indonesia said next week's meeting of key coffee producers in London was expected to delay taking a decision over fresh export quotas in view of gains in prices.
London robusta futures rallied to new one-year highs early Wednesday, but prices were off peaks by midday. LIFFE July was up $55 at the break, to $1,872, after ranging from $1,885 to $1,825.
